info.title: KUAA.IO API
info.summary: Identity verification, KYC, KYB and age checks for Brazil.
info.description:
The KUAA.IO API opens verification cases, adds the people and companies they are about, starts them on their pinned workflow and policy versions, and answers the decision and the dossier. Engines produce evidence; KUAA decides.

**Authentication.** Every operation takes the tenant's API key as `Authorization: Bearer kuaa_<prefix>_<secret>`. A key acts only in the tenant it was issued for and only with the scopes it was issued with; each operation lists the scopes it needs. A case of another tenant answers 404, the same as a case that does not exist.

**Idempotency.** Every POST, and PATCH /v1/cases/{id}, accepts an `Idempotency-Key`. The same key with the same request replays the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different request is 409.

**Errors.** Every error answers `{"error": {"code", "message", "fields"}}`. Branch on `code`; `fields` lists the messages per field of a rejected input (422).

**Brazilian identifiers.** CPF and CNPJ are text, never numbers. They are accepted with or without punctuation and answered normalized. The CNPJ is alphanumeric: twelve characters from 0-9 and A-Z followed by two check digits, `^[0-9A-Z]{12}[0-9]{2}$`. The dossier masks them down to their check digits unless the key holds `party.pii.view`.

## Sandbox

Every organization may have a **sandbox**: a test environment of its own, a separate tenant beside the live organization, opened by an admin in the backoffice. Its keys are `kuaa_test_<prefix>_<secret>`; a test key works only in the sandbox and a live key only in production. The sandbox answers the same operations, under the same scopes, workflows and policy versions (copied from production with the same digests), and no row of it is ever read by the live organization, nor the other way round.

In the sandbox every engine and every source is a **deterministic double**: no model is loaded, no list, registry or official source is consulted, and nothing is billed. Every answer says so: the response headers `Kuaa-Environment: sandbox` and `Kuaa-Livemode: false`, `livemode: false` on the case, run, decision and dossier, `environment` and `livemode` in every webhook, and `environment: sandbox`, `synthetic: true` in every piece of evidence. Webhooks of a sandbox are delivered for real, signed, over https, to an address that passed the same destination checks.

Captures are accepted as in production (JPEG or PNG, at least 64 pixels a side); the synthetic `/sandbox-documento.png` and `/sandbox-selfie.png` are ready to send. What a case comes to is chosen by the CPF or CNPJ of its parties, and any identifier not listed passes every check:

| Kind | Magic value | Scenario | What the engines answer | Decision (br.default v2) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPF | `000.000.001-91` | `clean` | Todas as verificações passam. | `approved` |
| CPF | `000.000.002-72` | `pep_match` | Triagem de PEP com correspondência forte (pep_match). | `manual_review` |
| CPF | `000.000.003-53` | `sanctions_match` | Triagem de sanções com correspondência confirmada (sanctions_confirmed). | `rejected` |
| CPF | `000.000.004-34` | `document_invalid` | Autenticidade do documento reprovada (document_invalid). | `rejected` |
| CPF | `000.000.005-15` | `face_mismatch` | Comparação facial abaixo da referência (face_mismatch). | `manual_review` |
| CPF | `000.000.006-04` | `liveness_inconclusive` | Prova de vida inconclusiva. | `manual_review` |
| CPF | `000.000.007-87` | `liveness_failed` | Prova de vida reprovada (liveness_failed). | `rejected` |
| CPF | `000.000.008-68` | `document_unreadable` | Captura do documento com qualidade insuficiente: pede nova captura. | `request_information` |
| CNPJ | `SA.NDB.OX0/0001-25` | `clean` | Empresa ativa, sócios sem correspondência e beneficiários resolvidos. | `approved` |
| CNPJ | `SA.NDB.OX0/0002-06` | `shell_indicators` | Quatro indicadores de empresa de fachada disparados (kyb.indicators.triggered_count = 4); a policy padrão não os lê. | `approved` |

get.description:
Answers one page of the cases of the key's organization, newest first -- by created_at, then by id -- with the filters combined. Each case is a summary with no party: no name, no CPF or CNPJ; read GET /v1/cases/{id} for its parties and custom status. Follow meta.next_cursor, with the same filters, for the next page; it is null on the last. The cursor is opaque and signed: an altered cursor, or one sent with other filters or by another organization, is 400 invalid_cursor. Paging never answers a case twice nor skips one older than the cursor, even while cases are opened. Filtering by tag needs `tag.list` as well.

**Required API key scopes:** `case.list`.

get.description:
Answers the links of the case, newest first, with their status, steps and expiry. A token is never answered here.

**The hosted capture.** The link opens `/c/<token>`, a page in Portuguese (pt-BR) headed by the brand of the organization that issued it -- the name, the logo and one accent of a closed set, as its administrators set them in the backoffice -- that asks, in order, for the consent, the document type (CIN, RG, CNH, the PDF of a digital CNH, passport), the front and back of the document through the camera or a file, a selfie with an active liveness challenge sequence drawn by the server -- two to four movements, shown one step at a time, each bound to its own nonce -- and a review. Which steps a link asks is read from the workflow version the case is pinned to; a case sent back for a new capture -- by the policy (`request_information`) or by a reviewer -- asks only for what answers why, with the reason in plain Portuguese. Sending the capture answers the case's waits for a capture or for information, so the workflow continues to its checks, publishes `capture_session.finished` to the webhook endpoints that subscribe to it (ids and the time only), and the link stops opening. The images are sealed as documents of the case; the sequence's measurements are recorded as evidence of the `liveness_challenge` check, a signal and never a verdict.

**Token.** `kc_` and 43 characters of base64url (256 bits), answered once; only its SHA-256 is stored. A newer link of the same case and party revokes the one before it. An unknown, expired, revoked or finished link answers the same 404 page, and an address that presents too many links that do not open is answered 429 for ten minutes.

**Embedding.** Without `embed_origin` the page refuses to be framed (`frame-ancestors 'none'`). With it, only that https origin may frame it -- an iframe with `allow="camera"`, or a WebView -- and the page posts `{type: "kuaa:step" | "kuaa:finished" | "kuaa:error", step}` to that origin, and to no other, with `window.parent.postMessage`. The events carry no personal data. Every capture page answers with its own `Content-Security-Policy` (script and style from the same origin only, images from the origin and blob:), `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self)` and `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`.

**Device.** The page reads the class of the device it is opened on -- `mobile`, `desktop` or `unknown` -- from what the browser says about itself (`Sec-CH-UA-Mobile` and the user agent, which is never stored). `handoff` -- the link's own, or the organization's setting, `suggest` by default -- decides how a desktop is offered the same link on a phone: `never`, no offer; `suggest`, the step with a QR code of the link and a button that copies or shares it (shown on a device that is not a desktop only when the page finds no camera); `require`, a desktop sees only the QR code, and that page tells it when the phone sent the capture. The organization may refuse device classes in the backoffice: a refused device is answered 403 with a page in Portuguese and, when a phone may open the link, its QR code. The QR code carries the same link: the token, its expiry and its limits do not change. The class the capture was sent from is recorded as the evidence of the `capture_device` check -- the facts `capture.device_class` and `capture.handed_off` -- a signal and never a verdict: a browser can say anything about itself.

**Status.** `GET /c/<token>/status` answers the page that embeds the link, or offered it on a phone, `{"data": {step, completed_steps, status, expires_at}}` as JSON under the same headers (`no-store`): `status` `active` with the step the person is on, or `finished` once sent. Any other link answers the same 404, and the same limit of links that do not open applies.

**Required API key scopes:** `capture_session.view`, `case.view`.

post.description:
Draws a fresh Active Authentication challenge for reading the passport chip of a person of the case -- the primary party when `party_id` is empty -- keeps it server-side, and answers its id and its eight bytes. A closed case is 409; a party that is not a person is 422.

**The passport chip (ICAO Doc 9303 eMRTD).** A browser cannot read the chip: a native app or SDK on the person's phone reads it over NFC, with BAC or PACE keyed by the printed MRZ. The flow is challenge, read, submit: ask for a challenge, send its eight bytes to the chip in INTERNAL AUTHENTICATE (Active Authentication), read EF.COM, EF.SOD, DG1, DG2, DG14, DG15 and EF.CardAccess (DG11 and DG12 when present), and post every file exactly as read -- tag and length included, in standard base64 -- with the chip's signature, what the device observed of Chip Authentication, the printed MRZ and the challenge_id. The server examines the files with arandu-emrtd against the CSCA trust store the deployment configured (EMRTD_CSCA_DIR): the data group hashes, the SOD signature, the chain Document Signer to CSCA, validity, revocation, the MRZ check digits, DG1 against the printed MRZ, Active Authentication against the server's own copy of the challenge, the Chip Authentication claim against DG14, and DG2 against the person's latest selfie. With no CSCA configured the chain is unverifiable, never passed. The read is recorded as the evidence of a `document_chip` check and its outcomes become the facts `chip.*` the policy reads; nothing is approved or rejected here. The raw files and the face image are sealed artifacts of the case. A challenge answers one read, once, before it expires (EMRTD_CHALLENGE_TTL_SECONDS, 300 by default); a used, expired or unknown challenge is 409 and records nothing. A hosted capture reads the chip at `/c/{token}/chip/desafio` and `/c/{token}/chip/leitura`, with the same bodies; see docs/nfc-chip.md.

**Required API key scopes:** `evidence.record`, `case.view`.

get.description:
Answers the endpoints of the key's tenant, by name. A secret is never answered here.

**Deliveries.** Each event a tenant's endpoint subscribes to -- `case.created`, `case.updated` (only when the status changed), `check.completed`, `decision.recorded`, `review.recorded`, `capture_session.finished`, `document.decided`, and the steps of a hosted capture -- `capture_session.opened`, `capture_session.consent_given`, `capture_session.document_submitted`, `capture_session.selfie_submitted`, `capture_session.expired`, `capture_session.revoked` -- is POSTed to the endpoint as one CloudEvents 1.0 event in the structured JSON mode (`Content-Type: application/json`): `specversion` "1.0", `type` the event name, `source` `urn:kuaa:tenant:<tenant_id>`, `id` the event id, `time` RFC 3339 UTC, `subject` `cases/<case_id>`, `datacontenttype` "application/json", and `data` with `event_id`, `type`, `occurred_at`, `tenant_id`, `case_id`, `status` (and `status_market`, the status in the market's vocabulary, on `case.created`, `case.updated` and `capture_session.finished`) and, for a check, a decision or a review, its `check_id`, `decision_id` or `review_id`; for `capture_session.finished`, sent once when the person sends a hosted capture, `status` `finished`, `capture_session_id` and `finished_at`; for `document.decided`, sent each time a reviewer decides about one document of a case, `status` and `decision` the decision (`approved`, `rejected` or `rerequested`), `document_decision_id`, `document_id`, `document_type` and `document_side` (absent for a selfie) and `requirement` -- never the reviewer's reason, and never a decision about the case; for the capture step events, `capture_session_id`, `status` the session's status after the event (`active`, `expired` or `revoked`) and, for consent, document and selfie, `step` (`consent`, `document`, `selfie`) -- `opened` is sent once, the first time the link opens on a device the organization allows; `consent_given` once; `document_submitted` and `selfie_submitted` each time one is stored; `expired` once, by a sweep every five minutes, for a link that passed its expiry unsent; `revoked` once, when a link that still opened is withdrawn or replaced by a newer link of the same party. They carry no device, no image and no token (schema `WebhookEvent`). `tenant_id` is the organization that issued the case and its links. It carries no personal data: it is a notification, and the case is read through `GET /v1/cases/{id}`.

**Signature.** Every attempt carries three headers: `X-Arandu-Delivery-Id`, the delivery id, the same on every retry; `X-Arandu-Timestamp`, the Unix time in seconds the attempt was signed at; and `X-Arandu-Signature`, `sha256=` followed by the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the endpoint's secret exactly as it was shown (its UTF-8 bytes, `whsec_` included), of the timestamp, a dot, the delivery id, a dot and the raw body. To verify a delivery: (1) read the body as bytes, before parsing it; (2) refuse a timestamp more than five minutes from your clock; (3) compute `sha256=` + hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + delivery_id + "." + body)); (4) compare it in constant time with each `X-Arandu-Signature` value -- after a rotation the previous secret keeps signing for 24 hours and the header comes once per secret, any one matching is enough; (5) only then parse the body, and deduplicate on its `id`, because delivery is at least once. Go receivers can call `webhook.Verify` from github.com/arandu-io/hesape/webhook.

**Retries.** An answer other than 2xx, or no answer, is tried again up to 5 attempts in all, 5 s, 30 s, 2 min and 10 min apart, honoring `Retry-After`; 408, 425, 429 and 5xx are retried and any other answer is final. Redirects are not followed. An endpoint whose deliveries give up 20 times in a row is turned off with `disabled_reason` `consecutive_failures`.

**Required API key scopes:** `webhook.manage`.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Register the https:// endpoints the case events are delivered to, signed, retried and logged. **Deliveries.** Each event a tenant's endpoint subscribes to -- `case.created`, `case.updated` (only when the status changed), `check.completed`, `decision.recorded`, `review.recorded`, `capture_session.finished`, `document.decided`, and the steps of a hosted capture -- `capture_session.opened`, `capture_session.consent_given`, `capture_session.document_submitted`, `capture_session.selfie_submitted`, `capture_session.expired`, `capture_session.revoked` -- is POSTed to the endpoint as one CloudEvents 1.0 event in the structured JSON mode (`Content-Type: application/json`): `specversion` "1.0", `type` the event name, `source` `urn:kuaa:tenant:<tenant_id>`, `id` the event id, `time` RFC 3339 UTC, `subject` `cases/<case_id>`, `datacontenttype` "application/json", and `data` with `event_id`, `type`, `occurred_at`, `tenant_id`, `case_id`, `status` (and `status_market`, the status in the market's vocabulary, on `case.created`, `case.updated` and `capture_session.finished`) and, for a check, a decision or a review, its `check_id`, `decision_id` or `review_id`; for `capture_session.finished`, sent once when the person sends a hosted capture, `status` `finished`, `capture_session_id` and `finished_at`; for `document.decided`, sent each time a reviewer decides about one document of a case, `status` and `decision` the decision (`approved`, `rejected` or `rerequested`), `document_decision_id`, `document_id`, `document_type` and `document_side` (absent for a selfie) and `requirement` -- never the reviewer's reason, and never a decision about the case; for the capture step events, `capture_session_id`, `status` the session's status after the event (`active`, `expired` or `revoked`) and, for consent, document and selfie, `step` (`consent`, `document`, `selfie`) -- `opened` is sent once, the first time the link opens on a device the organization allows; `consent_given` once; `document_submitted` and `selfie_submitted` each time one is stored; `expired` once, by a sweep every five minutes, for a link that passed its expiry unsent; `revoked` once, when a link that still opened is withdrawn or replaced by a newer link of the same party. They carry no device, no image and no token (schema `WebhookEvent`). `tenant_id` is the organization that issued the case and its links. It carries no personal data: it is a notification, and the case is read through `GET /v1/cases/{id}`.

**Signature.** Every attempt carries three headers: `X-Arandu-Delivery-Id`, the delivery id, the same on every retry; `X-Arandu-Timestamp`, the Unix time in seconds the attempt was signed at; and `X-Arandu-Signature`, `sha256=` followed by the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the endpoint's secret exactly as it was shown (its UTF-8 bytes, `whsec_` included), of the timestamp, a dot, the delivery id, a dot and the raw body. To verify a delivery: (1) read the body as bytes, before parsing it; (2) refuse a timestamp more than five minutes from your clock; (3) compute `sha256=` + hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + delivery_id + "." + body)); (4) compare it in constant time with each `X-Arandu-Signature` value -- after a rotation the previous secret keeps signing for 24 hours and the header comes once per secret, any one matching is enough; (5) only then parse the body, and deduplicate on its `id`, because delivery is at least once. Go receivers can call `webhook.Verify` from github.com/arandu-io/hesape/webhook.

**Retries.** An answer other than 2xx, or no answer, is tried again up to 5 attempts in all, 5 s, 30 s, 2 min and 10 min apart, honoring `Retry-After`; 408, 425, 429 and 5xx are retried and any other answer is final. Redirects are not followed. An endpoint whose deliveries give up 20 times in a row is turned off with `disabled_reason` `consecutive_failures`.
